whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Slack Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Implementation Consultants
personas.description: You roll out Slack for companies and design how teams, channels and workflows should be set up.

personas.label: Change Management Specialists
personas.description: You help people switch from email and old tools to Slack, and measure whether it is working.

personas.label: Salesforce Consultants
personas.description: You connect Slack to Sales Cloud and Service Cloud so teams can work on Salesforce data inside Slack.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Slack Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam, but it covers more than features. You need to know how to plan a Slack rollout, set it up securely, connect it to Salesforce, and get people to actually use it.
bullets: About 67% to pass, about 39 correct answers out of 60. Confirm it in the official exam guide before you book, since Salesforce updates these.
Wide scope. Workspace and channel design, Slack Connect, Workflow Builder, Salesforce integration and security.
People topics. Adoption planning, champions and success measures come up often.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: People who have run at least one Slack rollout, including the training and adoption work, do best. Before you book. Aim for 80% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Slack Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a company's situation, such as a merger, a security rule or slow adoption, and ask what the consultant should recommend.
bestWayToPass: Learn the structure: Workspaces, Enterprise Grid, channels, and how Slack Connect works with outside companies.
Know Workflow Builder: Triggers, steps and connectors, and when to use Salesforce Flow instead.
Understand the Salesforce link: The Salesforce apps for Slack and how records and alerts reach channels.
Plan for adoption: Champions, training, clear channel rules and how to measure success.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you plan and run a Slack rollout: workspace and channel design, workflows, Salesforce integration, security and governance, and getting people to use it. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 67% pass mark, weighted towards Policies and Settings (22%) and Learning and Enablement (18%).

keyConcepts.h2: Slack Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Salesforce-Slack Integration Architecture
blocks.body: Slack and Salesforce work together in several ways. The **Salesforce apps for Slack** let people search, view and update records, and get alerts, without leaving Slack. **Salesforce Flow** can post messages to Slack channels or create channels when something happens, such as a big deal closing. Teams can set up a channel per account or per major case, so everyone working on it talks in one place. **Agentforce** and AI features can also work inside Slack. Choose the simplest option that meets the need, and keep Salesforce as the system of record.

blocks.heading: Slack-First Customer Service Design
blocks.body: In customer service, Slack is often used for **swarming**: when a case is hard, the agent brings experts into a Slack channel linked to the case to solve it faster. Alerts about high-priority cases or missed service levels can go straight to the right channel. Knowledge shared in those channels can later become articles. The goal is faster answers for customers without agents having to chase people by email.

blocks.heading: Automations: Flow + Workflow Builder
blocks.body: **Workflow Builder** lets anyone build simple no-code workflows in Slack, such as a request form that posts to a channel and asks for approval. Workflows start from a **trigger**, like a shortcut, a new channel member or a schedule, and run **steps**, including connectors to other apps. For processes that change Salesforce data or need complex logic, **Salesforce Flow** is usually the better tool, and it can send results to Slack. Workflows should be owned and reviewed so they don't pile up unused.

blocks.heading: Data Governance and Compliance
blocks.body: Admins control how long messages and files are kept with **retention policies**. **Legal holds** and **eDiscovery** support legal requests. **Data loss prevention** can spot sensitive data, like card numbers, in messages. **Enterprise Key Management** lets a company control its own encryption keys, and **data residency** keeps data in a chosen region. Use **SSO** for login and **SCIM** to create and remove users automatically from the company's identity system. Set clear rules for who can create channels and invite outside people.

blocks.heading: Adoption Strategy and Change Management
blocks.body: A rollout only succeeds if people use Slack well. Start with clear goals and a few key use cases, like moving project chatter out of email. Recruit **champions** in each team to help others. Agree on **channel naming conventions** and when to use channels versus direct messages. Train people in short sessions focused on their work. Measure success with things like active users, messages in channels compared with DMs, and fewer internal emails, then adjust the plan.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Slack Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions describe a company and its goals or limits. Pick the recommendation that solves the real problem, often a people or process issue rather than a feature gap.

blocks.heading: Use Case Design
blocks.body: Start with a few high-value use cases tied to business goals, then expand. Don't try to move everything at once.

blocks.heading: Workflow Builder
blocks.body: Use Workflow Builder for simple Slack processes. Use Salesforce Flow when Salesforce data or complex logic is involved.

blocks.heading: Salesforce for Slack Integration
blocks.body: Bring records and alerts into the channels where people already work, and keep Salesforce as the source of truth.

blocks.heading: Adoption Strategy
blocks.body: Champions, training, clear channel rules and measured goals. Adoption problems are rarely solved by adding features.

blocks.heading: Governance Framework
blocks.body: Retention, legal hold, DLP, SSO, SCIM, and clear rules for channel creation and external sharing.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Slack Consultant:

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to work with an outside agency in shared Slack channels, without giving the agency accounts in its own workspace. What should be used?
options: A new workspace for the agency
Guest accounts for every agency employee
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack Connect lets two organisations share channels while each keeps its own workspace and controls.
whyWrong: A new workspace splits conversations and adds overhead.
Guest accounts can work but add admin effort and live in your workspace.
Email is what the company is trying to move away from.

sampleQuestions.question: Sales reps want an alert in their team channel when an opportunity over $1 million is closed in Salesforce. What is the best approach?
options: A Salesforce Flow posting to the channel
Ask each of the reps to post the update by hand
sampleQuestions.explanation: Flow can react to the record change in Salesforce and post to Slack automatically.
whyWrong: Manual posts get forgotten.
A daily email is slower and outside Slack.
A Workflow Builder form needs someone to fill it in.

sampleQuestions.question: Employees often send IT requests by DM, and nothing is tracked. What could a consultant recommend that needs no code?
options: A custom Slack application built by the in-house developers
A Workflow Builder form posting to an IT channel
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workflow Builder can collect requests in a form and post them to a channel where IT can track them.
whyWrong: Banning DMs doesn't create a request process.
A custom app is more than needed.
Weekly meetings are too slow for requests.

sampleQuestions.question: Legal requires that messages in certain channels are kept for seven years. What should be set?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retention policies control how long messages and files are kept.
whyWrong: Naming rules don't affect retention.
Slack Connect shares channels with others.
Workflows don't control retention.

sampleQuestions.question: When people leave the company, their Slack access should be removed automatically. What should be set up?
options: Manual removal carried out each month
sampleQuestions.explanation: SCIM lets the company's identity system create and remove Slack users automatically.
whyWrong: Retention policies cover data, not users.
Manual removal can be missed.
Naming conventions are for channels.

sampleQuestions.question: Six months after launch, many teams still use email for projects. What should the consultant focus on first?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slow adoption is usually a people and process issue. Champions and clear guidance help most.
whyWrong: Turning off email harms the business.
More apps don't change habits.
Licences don't drive use.

sampleQuestions.question: Which measure best shows that teams are working in the open in Slack?
options: The share of messages in channels rather than DMs
The total number of apps that have been installed
sampleQuestions.explanation: More messages in channels means more work is visible and searchable.
whyWrong: Emoji count doesn't show how work happens.
Workspace count isn't a usage measure.
App count doesn't show adoption.

sampleQuestions.question: A support agent is stuck on a complex case and needs help from engineering. What Slack-based approach fits?
options: Swarming: a channel on the case with the experts in it
Close the existing case and then open an entirely new one
Wait for the next team meeting
sampleQuestions.explanation: Swarming brings the right people together in a channel to solve the case quickly.
whyWrong: Email is slower and harder to follow.
Closing the case loses history.
Waiting delays the customer.

sampleQuestions.question: People can't find the right channels because names are all different. What should the consultant recommend?
options: A naming convention with clear prefixes
Deleting the majority of the channels
sampleQuestions.explanation: Naming conventions, such as proj- or team- prefixes, make channels easy to find and understand.
whyWrong: A new workspace doesn't fix naming.
Deleting channels loses history.
More DMs make work less visible.

sampleQuestions.question: Messages must be scanned to stop people posting credit card numbers. What should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data loss prevention can detect and act on sensitive data in messages.
whyWrong: Naming conventions don't scan content.
Huddles are for audio and video calls.
Forms collect input, they don't scan messages.

sampleQuestions.question: A company has many business units, each needing its own workspace but with shared company-wide channels. What fits?
options: Slack Connect set up between the separate business units
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enterprise Grid lets one company run several connected workspaces with shared channels and central controls.
whyWrong: One channel for everyone is unworkable.
Slack Connect is for outside organisations.
Unconnected workspaces can't share channels easily.

sampleQuestions.question: A process needs to update several Salesforce records with complex rules when someone approves a request in Slack. What is the better tool?
options: Workflow Builder used entirely on its own
Salesforce Flow, with Slack for the message
sampleQuestions.explanation: Flow handles complex Salesforce logic, and it can still use Slack for the approval step.
whyWrong: Pinned messages don't automate anything.
Workflow Builder is best for simple Slack-side processes.
Reminders don't update records.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to control its own encryption keys for Slack data. What should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enterprise Key Management lets the company manage the keys used to encrypt its Slack data.
whyWrong: Slack Connect shares channels.
Retention controls how long data is kept.
SCIM manages user accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should a Slack rollout start?
options: Clear goals and a few high-value use cases
Installing as many apps as possible
Moving every single tool into Slack on the first day
sampleQuestions.explanation: Starting with goals and a few use cases gives quick wins and something to measure.
whyWrong: Turning off email is disruptive and unnecessary.
Lots of apps add noise.
Moving everything at once overwhelms people.

sampleQuestions.question: Sales reps want to look up and update Salesforce opportunities without leaving Slack. What should be set up?
options: A Workflow Builder form for each opportunity
A daily export to a channel
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce app for Slack lets people search, view and update records from Slack.
whyWrong: A form per opportunity is impractical.
Reminders don't show records.
A daily export is out of date and read-only.
